benchmark_cost.definition: per benchmark, mean over models with an observed cell of the per-(model, benchmark) value; cost_tokens = sum over the cell's few-shot runs (runs.json) and their sub_splits of num_instances x (num_prompt_tokens + num_output_tokens), one pass (one in-context-example trial), model-specific tokenizers
benchmark_cost.requests_per_instance_note: median over models of num_requests / (instances x trials summed over all splits and perturbed copies), from runs.json; 1 where every run uses generation or multiple_choice_joint and runs.json reports no num_requests

BoolQ.group_description: The BoolQ benchmark for binary (yes/no) question answering [(Clark et al., 2019)](https://aclanthology.org/N19-1300/).
BoolQ.metric_description: Fraction of instances that the predicted output matches a correct reference up to light processing.

CNN/DailyMail.group_description: The CNN/DailyMail benchmark for text summarization ([Hermann et al., 2015](https://papers.nips.cc/paper/2015/hash/afdec7005cc9f14302cd0474fd0f3c96-Abstract.html); [Nallapati et al.,2016](https://aclanthology.org/K16-1028/)).
CNN/DailyMail.metric_description: Average ROUGE score [(Lin, 2004)](https://aclanthology.org/W04-1013/) based on 2-gram overlap.

CivilComments.group_description: The CivilComments benchmark for toxicity detection [(Borkan et al., 2019)](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1903.04561.pdf).
CivilComments.metric_description: Fraction of instances that the predicted output matches a correct reference up to light processing.

HellaSwag.group_description: The HellaSwag benchmark for commonsense reasoning in question answering [(Zellers et al., 2019)](https://aclanthology.org/P19-1472/).
HellaSwag.metric_description: Fraction of instances that the predicted output matches a correct reference exactly.

IMDB.group_description: The IMDB benchmark for sentiment analysis in movie review [(Maas et al., 2011)](https://aclanthology.org/P11-1015/).
IMDB.metric_description: Fraction of instances that the predicted output matches a correct reference up to light processing.

MMLU.group_description: The Massive Multitask Language Understanding (MMLU) benchmark for knowledge-intensive question answering across 57 domains [(Hendrycks et al., 2021)](https://openreview.net/forum?id=d7KBjmI3GmQ).
MMLU.metric_description: Fraction of instances that the predicted output matches a correct reference exactly.

MS MARCO (TREC).group_description: The MS MARCO benchmark's deep learning TREC track for passage retrieval in information retrieval [(https://trec.nist.gov)](https://microsoft.github.io/msmarco/).
MS MARCO (TREC).metric_description: Normalized discounted cumulative gain at 10 in information retrieval.

MS MARCO (regular).group_description: The MS MARCO benchmark's regular track for passage retrieval in information retrieval [(https://microsoft.github.io/msmarco/)](https://microsoft.github.io/msmarco/).
MS MARCO (regular).metric_description: Mean reciprocal rank at 10 in information retrieval.

NarrativeQA.group_description: The NarrativeQA benchmark for reading comprehension over narratives [(Kočiský et al., 2017)](https://aclanthology.org/Q18-1023/).
NarrativeQA.metric_description: Average F1 score in terms of word overlap between the model output and correct reference.

NaturalQuestions (closed-book).group_description: The NaturalQuestions [(Kwiatkowski et al., 2019)](https://aclanthology.org/Q19-1026/) benchmark for question answering based on naturally-occurring queries through Google Search. The input does not include the Wikipedia page with the answer.
NaturalQuestions (closed-book).metric_description: Average F1 score in terms of word overlap between the model output and correct reference.

NaturalQuestions (open-book).group_description: The NaturalQuestions [(Kwiatkowski et al., 2019)](https://aclanthology.org/Q19-1026/) benchmark for question answering based on naturally-occurring queries through Google Search. The input includes the Wikipedia page with the answer.
NaturalQuestions (open-book).metric_description: Average F1 score in terms of word overlap between the model output and correct reference.

OpenbookQA.group_description: The OpenbookQA benchmark for commonsense-intensive open book question answering [(Mihaylov et al., 2018)](https://aclanthology.org/D18-1260/).
OpenbookQA.metric_description: Fraction of instances that the predicted output matches a correct reference exactly.

QuAC.group_description: The QuAC benchmark for question answering in the context of dialogues [(Choi et al., 2018)](https://aclanthology.org/D18-1241/).
QuAC.metric_description: Average F1 score in terms of word overlap between the model output and correct reference.

RAFT.group_description: The Real-world annotated few-shot (RAFT) meta-benchmark of 11 real-world text classification tasks [(Alex et al., 2021)](https://datasets-benchmarks-proceedings.neurips.cc/paper/2021/hash/ca46c1b9512a7a8315fa3c5a946e8265-Abstract-round2.html).
RAFT.metric_description: Fraction of instances that the predicted output matches a correct reference up to light processing.

TruthfulQA.group_description: The TruthfulQA benchmarking for measuring model truthfulness and commonsense knowledge in question answering [(Lin et al., 2022)](https://aclanthology.org/2022.acl-long.229/).
TruthfulQA.metric_description: Fraction of instances that the predicted output matches a correct reference exactly.

XSUM.group_description: The XSUM benchmark for text summarization of BBC news articles [(Narayan et al., 2018)](https://aclanthology.org/D18-1206/).
XSUM.metric_description: Average ROUGE score [(Lin, 2004)](https://aclanthology.org/W04-1013/) based on 2-gram overlap.

caveats: Scores and costs come from the few-shot leaderboard runs in runs.json. In 19 cells HELM's leaderboard table also pools a zero-shot ablation run (max_train_instances=0) into the cell: TruthfulQA for Anthropic-LM v4-s3, BLOOM, GLM, GPT-J, GPT-NeoX, OPT 175B, OPT 66B, T0pp, T5, UL2, YaLM, and CNN/DailyMail + XSUM for curie, davinci, text-curie-001, text-davinci-002. There B is the few-shot value and differs from the HELM website by up to 0.0135; HELM's value is kept in leaderboard_differences and cell_costs.leaderboard_value.
Scores are means over 3 in-context-example trials for most cells (1 trial for HellaSwag, OpenbookQA and 25 of the 30 models added in 2023); cell_costs.num_train_trials. Costs are for one trial.
Fill is 81.7%: HellaSwag, OpenbookQA (32 models), MS MARCO (30/31) and the two summarization scenarios (42) were not run for every model.

Anthropic-LM v4-s3 (52B) has complete 3-trial MS MARCO (regular) and (TREC) runs in runs.json (RR@10 0.382, NDCG@10 0.642), but HELM's leaderboard shows no value for them; they are left missing as published and listed in consistency.runs_json_values_missing_from_leaderboard.
HELM marks 58 cells as contaminated (54 weak, 4 strong, e.g. T0pp); scores are kept and flagged in cell_costs.contamination_level.

CivilComments: HELM's tables average the toxic/non-toxic sub-splits without weights ('# eval' is half the instance count); here instances, token means and times are instance-weighted over the sub-splits from runs.json (cell_costs.instances_table keeps the table's '# eval').

HellaSwag (multiple_choice_separate_original), OpenbookQA (_calibrated) and MS MARCO (ranking_binary) send several requests per instance (4, 8, 30.5 and 224.6); cost_tokens counts one request per instance as specified, benchmark_cost.cost_tokens_requests_mean multiplies by requests_per_instance.
OpenbookQA's reported '# prompt tokens' (~5) appears to cover only the calibration requests, so its token cost is underestimated even after the request correction.

num_requests (runs.json) is reported only for the 37 original 2022 models; the 30 models added in 2023 (LLaMA, Llama 2, Falcon, Jurassic-2, gpt-3.5-turbo, ...) lack the stat. It counts all splits, trials and perturbed copies of a run.
Ten old model ids (together/bloom, together/opt-175b, ...) are missing from model_metadata.yaml and were matched by display name (release_date_source).
Data license unresolved: HELM's code is Apache-2.0, but the benchmark_output JSON states no terms for redistributing the score tables; check before the data release.

Raw inputs are pinned by GCS object generation, but the bucket keeps only the current generation (HELM rewrote all release files in 2026). After HELM's next rewrite '--fetch --pin-manifest' will fail; the sha256 values (source.raw_inputs, raw_manifests/<name>.json) then only verify archived copies, so the raw directory (~92 MB for the three HELM matrices) should be archived with the data release.

cell_costs.layout: lists [model][benchmark] aligned with model_names x benchmark_names; null where unobserved (leaderboard_value: HELM's displayed score, only where it differs from B)

release_date_vs_model_id.rule: a release date conflicts with the date in the model id if it is more than 7 days earlier or more than 60 days later (YYMM ids: than the month), or, for OpenAI MMDD ids, has another month-day

runs_json_cross_check.note: runs.json value of each observed cell (the cell's runs; see score_definition) vs the leaderboard value, and runs.json costs vs leaf-table costs; cost differences are expected only in leaderboard_differences cells and in cells with sub_splits (CivilComments)

consistency.scores_source: runs.json few-shot leaderboard runs (HELM's displayed value where equal within SCORE_TOL)

name: helm_classic
order: rows: HELM display names sorted by Python str order (Unicode code points); columns: benchmark names sorted the same way
score_definition: the scenario's main metric on its main split over the cell's few-shot leaderboard runs in runs.json (data_augmentation=canonical; no ablation, contrast, zero-shot max_train_instances=0 or duplicate device runs), merged as HELM merges stats (sum / count over trial entries: mean over sub-runs and the in-context-example trials). Equal to the release leaderboard 'Accuracy' table value (kept bit for bit) except in leaderboard_differences, where HELM's table also pools a zero-shot run

source.license: HELM code is Apache-2.0 (github.com/stanford-crfm/helm); the benchmark_output JSON states no separate data license
